messages.subject: To identify person parameter correctly
parts:
Hi Phil
From mirt package, I learn a lot (multidimensional item response theory). Thanks.
I have some question to solve
The simdata function, how can I get the simulate person parameter ?
For example, In Reference manual(version 1.1) page 6-7, mixed itemtype example
simdata(a,d,2000,itemtype=items,sigma=sigma)
how can I get the simulate person parameter?
And, besides item parameters, person parameter estimation
can get from the fscore, right?
I  want to make sure that estimated person parameters are not 
far from the true parameters.
Best
Chun-Hsien Wu

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: To identify person parameter correctly
parts:
Hi Chun-Hsien,

The best strategy is to use the Theta = argument to simdata(), and input a matrix you simulated. For example,

Theta <- matrix(rnorm(1000))
dat = simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich', Theta=Theta)

Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: To identify person parameter correctly
parts:
Hi Chun-Hsein,

When you consider the number of items, this makes perfect sense. You
have only 11 items to identify 3 cross-loaded factors, which means
that the amount of information any one item tells you about a factor
is even less than the unidimensional case. The RMSD makes sense here
as well, where the lowest difference occurs for the factor with the
largest number of loadings.

> sqrt(apply((fullscores - Theta)^2, 2, mean))
F1 F2 F3
0.6842767 1.0985522 0.9480303


And when you consider the marginal reliability estimates by calling
just fscores() by itself:


> x = fscores(simmod)

Method: EAP

Empirical Reliability:
F1 F2 F3
0.6154 0.1859 0.2402


It's easy to see that the factors are pretty unreliable, and therefore
the factor scores (i.e., true-scores) are going to be measured with a
large amount of imprecision. The more items you have in a test the
more accurate you can measure factors, and factors with a smaller
number of loadings will naturally have less precision as well.


Phil
